name: matches a stable dense reference
input: rectangular noncontiguous float32/float64 tensors and uneven/oversized tiles
test:
import math
import torch
torch.manual_seed(493)
for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
    Q = torch.randn(5,6,dtype=dtype)[:,::2]
    K = torch.randn(7,6,dtype=dtype)[:,::2]
    V = torch.randn(7,4,dtype=dtype)[:,::2]
    before = [x.clone() for x in (Q,K,V)]
    expected = (Q @ K.T / math.sqrt(3)).softmax(-1) @ V
    for b in (1,2,3,20):
        out = blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,b)
        assert isinstance(out,torch.Tensor) and out.shape == (5,2)
        assert out.dtype == dtype and out.device == Q.device
        torch.testing.assert_close(out,expected,rtol=2e-5,atol=2e-6)
    assert all(torch.equal(x,old) for x,old in zip((Q,K,V),before))
out = blockwise_attention([[1.]],[[1.],[0.]],[[2.],[4.]],1)
torch.testing.assert_close(out,torch.tensor([[2.53788284]]))

name: large scores remain finite
input: online maxima change across key tiles and value width differs from feature width
test:
import torch
Q=torch.tensor([[1000.],[-1000.],[0.]])
K=torch.tensor([[-1.],[0.],[1.]])
V=torch.tensor([[-5.,6.],[3.,4.],[7.,2.]])
expected=torch.tensor([[7.,2.],[-5.,6.],[5./3.,4.]])
for b in (1,2,10):
    out=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,b)
    assert isinstance(out,torch.Tensor) and torch.isfinite(out).all()
    torch.testing.assert_close(out,expected)

name: gradients and device match dense attention
input: all Q/K/V gradients for multiple tile sizes
test:
import math
import torch
torch.manual_seed(494)
for device in (['cpu','cuda'] if torch.cuda.is_available() else ['cpu']):
    Q=torch.randn(3,2,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
    K=torch.randn(5,2,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
    V=torch.randn(5,4,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
    probe=torch.randn(3,4,dtype=torch.float64,device=device)
    expected=(Q@K.T/math.sqrt(2)).softmax(-1)@V
    grads=torch.autograd.grad((expected*probe).sum(),(Q,K,V))
    for b in (1,2,9):
        actual=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,b)
        assert actual.dtype==Q.dtype and actual.device==Q.device and actual.requires_grad
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual,expected)
        actual_grads=torch.autograd.grad((actual*probe).sum(),(Q,K,V))
        for actual_grad,expected_grad in zip(actual_grads,grads):
            torch.testing.assert_close(actual_grad,expected_grad,rtol=1e-9,atol=1e-10)

name: computes only bounded score tiles without attention helpers
input: both axes exceed tile size; dispatch observes matmul intermediates
test:
import math
import torch
from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode
class TileGuard(TorchDispatchMode):
    def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
        assert 'scaled_dot_product' not in str(func), 'attention helper is not allowed'
        result=func(*args,**(kwargs or {}))
        if func in (torch.ops.aten.mm.default,torch.ops.aten.bmm.default,torch.ops.aten.addmm.default):
            assert result.shape[-2]<=2 and result.shape[-1]<=2, 'matmul exceeded score tile bound'
        return result
torch.manual_seed(495)
Q=torch.randn(7,3,dtype=torch.float64)
K=torch.randn(11,3,dtype=torch.float64)
V=torch.randn(11,1,dtype=torch.float64)
expected=(Q@K.T/math.sqrt(3)).softmax(-1)@V
with TileGuard():
    actual=blockwise_attention(Q,K,V,2)
torch.testing.assert_close(actual,expected)
